description:
Impacted As-Planned (IAP) on an unprogressed as-planned
            baseline. Implements AACE RP 29R-03 MIP 3.6 (Modeled /
            Additive / Single Base) and SCL Protocol 2nd ed. §11.6(a).
            Two modes.

            **screen** (default): inserts each delay fragnet into the
            as-planned baseline, first one at a time and then all together,
            re-runs CPM, and reads the joint impact against verdict bands
            (NO SIGNAL, LOW SIGNAL, MODERATE SIGNAL, STRONG SIGNAL, or
            INDETERMINATE when the joint pass fails). Use it as a quick read
            on whether a delay claim has legs before a fuller analysis. The
            sum of the one-at-a-time impacts is reported beside the joint
            impact; ``overstatement_days`` is the difference, from fragnets
            that share a path. Check each ``per_fragnet[].status`` before
            quoting a figure: a fragnet that failed on its own carries
            ``status`` "error" and its ``error``, and is left out of the
            one-at-a-time sum. The joint pass inserts every fragnet
            together, so read ``joint.status`` and the "iap-joint" warnings
            too: with a bad fragnet the joint pass can fail (verdict
            INDETERMINATE) or run without the ties it could not insert.

            **rebut**: tests an opposing expert's IAP submission. Supply at
            least one of: ``opposing_impacted_xer_path`` or
            ``opposing_impacted_xer_content`` (tier A: re-runs their
            impacted schedule and diffs it against the baseline),
            ``opposing["fragnets"]`` (tier B: re-models their fragnets on
            the baseline), or ``opposing["claimed_impact_days"]`` (tier C:
            their stated figure).

            IAP does not look at what actually happened on site: it
            measures the planned logic plus the inserted delays. The result
            carries ``iap_method_caveat`` saying so, and a ``precondition``
            block that flags a baseline carrying progress (not a pure
            as-planned schedule). Every activity is laid out on one uniform
            timeline with no weekends or holidays, each timeline day being
            one working day of that activity's own calendar. Where every
            unfinished activity is on one calendar, each impact is exact in
            working days on it, apart from constraint dates and any stretch
            before the data date, which the run places on the project's
            default calendar. With more than one calendar, paths on
            different calendars change length against each other on that
            timeline, so float, the driving path and the impact can differ
            from a calendar-aware run, and the impact is a mix of those
            calendars' working days; the result lists the calendars
            (``calendars_in_use``, and ``opposing_calendars_in_use`` for a
            tier A file) and warns when there is more than one. The absolute
            dates the run shows are not P6 calendar dates (``date_basis``):
            quote the day counts, not the dates. For an impact measured on each event's own
            contemporaneous baseline use ``time_impact_analysis_fragnet``
            (MIP 3.7); for retrospective windows use
            ``forensic_windows_analysis`` (MIP 3.3); for a subtractive
            but-for use ``collapsed_as_built`` (MIP 3.8).

            Args:
                baseline_xer_path:    server-side as-planned baseline XER.
                baseline_xer_content: full text of the as-planned baseline
                                      XER (alternative for hosted/remote use).
                                      Supply EXACTLY ONE of path/content.
                fragnets: SCREEN (required): list of fragnet dicts, each
                    with ``id``, ``name``, ``liability`` (responsible
                    party), ``activities`` (list of {code, name,
                    duration_days}; duration_days in working days) and
                    ``ties`` (list of {from_code, to_code, type, lag_days};
                    pred/succ are accepted aliases for from_code/to_code;
                    type is FS, SS, FF or SF in any case, with or without
                    P6's PR_ prefix; a missing type is FS and any other
                    type is refused).
                mode: "screen" (default) or "rebut" (case does not matter).
                opposing: REBUT: dict of the opposing material, with any of
                    ``fragnets`` (same shape as above),
                    ``claimed_impact_days`` (number), ``claimed_finish``
                    (YYYY-MM-DD), ``proj_id``, ``expert_name``,
                    ``report_ref``. Other keys are refused. Pass the
                    opposing impacted schedule through the two arguments
                    below, not in this dict.
                opposing_impacted_xer_path:    REBUT tier A: server-side
                                               opposing impacted XER.
                opposing_impacted_xer_content: REBUT tier A: full text of
                                               the opposing impacted XER.
                                               Supply at most ONE of this
                                               path/content pair.
                own_results: REBUT, optional: your own results from the
                    primary methods in working days, {windows_days,
                    tia_days, collapsed_days}, read beside the opposing
                    figure.
                proj_id: optional project selector inside a multi-project
                    baseline XER.
                screen_bands: SCREEN, optional: verdict band overrides,
                    {low_pct, strong_pct, wd_floor_moderate}. Defaults
                    2.0, 5.0 and 20; low_pct must stay below strong_pct.
                baseline_name / opposing_name: optional file names to
                    print in the report for XERs sent as content (a
                    content upload has no file name of its own).
                preparer / company: optional, printed on the report and
                    dashboard as who prepared the analysis. Both are blank
                    unless supplied.
                output_dir: output dir for the HTML dashboard, TXT report
                    and CSVs (tempdir if "").
                project_name: optional override.

            Limits for hosted use: 500 fragnets on each side, and 5,000
            inserted activities and 20,000 ties across all of them.

            Returns:
                {
                  "mode": "screen" | "rebut",
                  "method": "Impacted As-Planned — AACE 29R-03 §3.6 / MIP 3.6 ...",
                  "baseline": {project_finish, plan_start,
                               baseline_duration_wd, critical_count, ...},
                  "precondition": {progressed_count, total_count,
                                   pure_as_planned},
                  "per_fragnet": [{fragnet_id, status, error,
                                   impact_days, impact_working_days, ...}],  # SCREEN
                  "joint": {status, impact_days, impact_working_days, ...},  # SCREEN
                  "sum_isolated_days": int,           # SCREEN
                  "sum_isolated_working_days": int,   # SCREEN
                  "overstatement_days": int,          # SCREEN: sum minus joint
                  "screen_verdict": {band, pct, joint_wd, bands_used, basis},  # SCREEN
                  "rebut": {...},         # REBUT: tiers A/B/C and findings
                  "critique": {...},
                  "iap_method_caveat": str,
                  "date_basis": str,
                  "day_unit_basis": str,  # what every day count counts
                  "calendars_in_use": [str] | None,  # None: could not be read
                  "opposing_calendars_in_use": [str] | None,  # REBUT tier A
                  "output_files": {report, events_csv, dashboard, ...},
                  "warnings": [...],
                  "baseline_sha256": str, "baseline_sha256_basis": str,
                  "opposing_impacted_sha256": str,        # REBUT tier A
                  "opposing_impacted_sha256_basis": str,  # REBUT tier A
                }
name: impacted_as_planned
